touches.text: Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Has its own workflow stamped on it (the state string, with the cursor).
Each workflow step declares what it needs.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are housed in harbor_master.
"HARBOR MASTER IS A REPORTING SYSTEM AND NOTHING MORE. IT REPORTS WHERE EVERYTHING IS AND NOTHING ELSE PERIOD. THATS ITS INTENTION."

"it owns the gates only because we had to have some place to put them, but it does not control anything." The gates refuse on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10: "the gate is the refuser but it's doing so on behalf of the ticket. so the ticket owns the refusal.")
VERBS: crossing, watch, clear. clear is the PROVED gate it houses on the ticket's behalf.
artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). USERS: everyone who writes a record.
gate: the == compare, in one place. A gate opens when every expected equals its actual. No oracle, ever.

ROOT INTENTION for checks and gates (Akien, 2026-10-27): the inspector does all the checks, so there is no need for more checks anywhere else. The inspector's output is consumed by the gate. The gate's output is the certificate. "This was how I meant it all along."
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.

The crossing is the ticket's own act. The gate's probe (the same kind that sends notice of gate passage) tells the passing ticket "you can now advance to X", and the ticket updates itself. (Q#61, Akien 2026-10-27)
